sections.content: It is kind of difficult for students like me who miss some classes. But if you attend full classes, it is easy to understand.
sections.teaching: Pedro is really good! His speaking is easy to understand and he gives humorous examples in class.
sections.grading: Pedro is really generous in terms of grading. I know students who scored only 40-50(full score 100) got a B+. So get a A is also easy. What's more, Pedro outlines the keypoints before the exam for students to better review the course. I really love it!
sections.workload: Very very little workload, only need to finish a project.

sections.content:
Two parts: rendering and geometry. The PPT and materials can be found at https://course.cse.ust.hk/comp5411.

- Rendering Architecture
- The rendering pipeline and GPU architecture
- Transformation mathematics
- GPU pipeline stages (vertex, raster, fragment)
- Programming with WebGL/GLSL
- Texture filtering
- Framebuffer operations
- Shadow algorithms
- Geometry Processing
- Mesh representations
- Parametric surfaces: Bézier, NURBS, subdivision schemes
- Remeshing & parameterization
- Level-of-Detail (LOD) systems
- GPU hardware tessellation
- Data Representation and Rendering Models
(subject to updates and if time permits)
- Physics-based rendering and Global illumination
- Other representations (e.g., volumetric, neural)
- Additional Topics on animation, simulation, VR
sections.teaching: The professor's class is very interesting and passionate. The professor speaks at a moderate pace, so even for someone like me who isn't very good at English, it's easy to understand. The course content is engaging, and there is often interaction.
sections.grading:
The grading are consisted of a project and the final exam. The project and be done in a group of 1 or 2. The details can be found at https://course.cse.ust.hk/comp5411 .

9% Project Proposal (A1)
9% Project Progress (A2 and Demo)
30% Project Result (A3)
10% Participation (F1,F2,F3,F4 and Zoom comments)
42% Final Exam
sections.workload: The workload depends on the projects you choose. The professor said that as long as it's related to rendering or geometry, or even related to your research, any project connected to graphics is acceptable. You can discuss with the professor what topics to do. I feel there is a lot of flexibility, so the workload really depends on the projects you take on, as there are no regular assignments.

sections.content: This course consists of two parts. The first part (by  Prof. Chiew-Lan Tai) covers topics in geometric representations, modeling and processing, and the second part (by Prof. Pedro Sander) covers topics in geometry rendering, lighting, and shading, using latest generation graphics hardware.
sections.teaching: The contents of both parts are intersting and useful. Prof. Chiew-Lan Tai's class makes me sleepy while Prof. Pedro Sander's class is much more attractive.
sections.grading: I am not sure how many students get B+ or above but the ratio seems high.
sections.workload:
The first part: 2 assignments and 1 project
The second part: a project with 2 presentations
